key_insight: Whole-genome sequencing in Latin American patients with early-onset or familial Parkinson’s disease uncovered additional pathogenic and likely pathogenic variants that standard genotyping could miss.
clinical_relevance: Broader genomic screening may improve genetic diagnosis and counseling for early-onset/familial Parkinson’s disease in underrepresented Latin American populations.
method: Short-read whole-genome sequencing was performed in 263 individuals with early-onset PD and/or a family history of PD.
Participants were selected after prior genotyping showed no known pathogenic PD variant.
Variants were screened across 7 PD-related genes and 21 genes linked to related parkinsonian disorders.
evidence_signal: Among analyzed individuals, 4.7% had pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants in primary or secondary PD genes, 5.5% had pathogenic/likely pathogenic Gaucher disease variants, and 2.7% carried known GBA1 risk variants.
watch_item: This was a selected subset without known pathogenic variants on prior genotyping, so the findings may not generalize to all PD patients and still require careful variant interpretation.
paper_title: Genomic Landscape of Early-Onset and Familial Latin American Parkinson's Patients
